meta.description: Designs and analyzes combinatorial CRISPR screens covering paired-Cas9, Cas12a multiplex, genetic-interaction scoring, and MAGeCK MLE interaction analysis.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated citations, datasets, clinical results, or numerical results were introduced in the nine executions.

practice_boundaries.detail: The explicit Scope note limits screen calls to research leads and rejects patient-treatment inference.

methodological_ground.detail: The primary GI workflow now requires BH-FDR for genome-scale calls and directs raw-score ranking for small hand-curated sets.

code_usability.detail: The shipped GI example ran on fresh data; MAGeCK MLE and the in4mer helper also executed and produced asserted outputs.

functional_suitability.note: The architecture, GI, MLE, and in4mer workflows are present and executed. The usage guide still tells agents to apply a raw z=-2 cutoff without carrying forward the primary Skill's genome-scale BH-FDR safeguard.

reliability.note: Missing-singleton handling, low-N guidance, and the MAGeCK FDR reproducibility warning are explicit; malformed count/design inputs still rely mainly on raw tool errors.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is concise and the usage guide points to primary sections rather than duplicating long tables.

agent_usability.note: The decision table, runnable example, and error modes are clear. The raw-cutoff wording in usage-guide.md is inconsistent with the genome-scale FDR instruction in SKILL.md.

human_usability.note: Prompts and prerequisite data are clear; invalid MAGeCK inputs lack a Skill-level recovery path.

security.note: No credentials, unsafe dynamic execution, or sensitive-data retention mechanism is present.

maintainability.note: The main GI implementation is a tested example and version checks are documented. There is no automated test harness, and one numerical simulation claim was not reproducible from its stated model.

agent_specific.note: Triggering and scope escape hatches are strong. MAGeCK permutation FDR is inherently non-idempotent, though accurately disclosed; the usage guide needs the same FDR escape hatch.

key_strengths: The shipped GI example runs on fresh cassette-level data and recovers known truth with BH-FDR control.
The updated primary Skill correctly distinguishes small hand-curated sets from genome-scale FDR-controlled calls.
The MAGeCK MLE design matrix is executable and explicitly documents permutation-FDR non-reproducibility.
The research-only scope boundary prevents patient-level treatment interpretation.

recommendations.title: Carry BH-FDR guidance into usage guide
recommendations.problem: usage-guide.md still asks agents to apply a raw z=-2 cutoff in its example prompt and workflow step, without the genome-scale BH-FDR qualification now present in SKILL.md.
recommendations.root_cause: The final-pass correction changed SKILL.md and examples/gi_scoring.py but did not update the abbreviated usage-guide workflow.
recommendations.fix: Revise the GI prompt and workflow step to state that raw z classification is only for small hand-curated sets; for genome-scale screens require two-sided z p-values and BH-FDR before calling hits.

recommendations.title: Reproduce or qualify minimum-N percentages
recommendations.problem: The stated approximately 4% N=20 and 0.5% N=30 miss rates did not reproduce in a fresh 1,000-replicate run of the stated two-hit, GI=-2.5, null-SD=0.4 model; both were 0/2000 in this run.
recommendations.root_cause: The narrative gives precise rates without shipping the generating simulation or enough parameter detail to reproduce its variance model.
recommendations.fix: Either ship the exact simulation and seed used for the percentages or replace the precise N=20/N=30 rates with a qualitative caution while retaining the conservative N>=50 recommendation.
